findings.summary: Attention still spends 90.2% in OCR. Four proposals yield only 1.01–1.11 tokens per verification step; GPU token work remains uneven.
observations: The four-proposal configuration uses the original four L4 GPUs, server concurrency eight, compiled BF16 embeddings, region window 64, dynamic pages and frozen references. One warm-up, three ordinary calls and a separate instrumented full call completed.

Median diagnostic latency is 3.036 s, with OCR 2.731 s and embedding 0.192 s. Percentage shares use mean times: 90.2% OCR and 6.2% embedding. These diagnostic calls are separate from evaluator samples.

Proposal acceptance across ordinary-call counters is 0.88%, 0.31%, 2.79% and 2.47% on GPUs 0–3. Including the bonus token, mean emitted tokens per verification step are 1.035, 1.012, 1.112 and 1.099. Census GPU 3 achieved 1.60 in its corresponding study; speculation helps the two workloads differently.

All ordinary calls produced 67 regions. In two calls, GPU token totals were [1077, 455, 717, 1482]; the third was [913, 454, 854, 1510]. Each GPU handled 16–17 regions. Similar region counts still left roughly 3.3 times as much generated-token work on GPU 3 as GPU 1.

OCR-window GPU busy observations average [94.8, 80.7, 82.0, 97.5]% on GPUs 0–3. Only six one-second observations per GPU fall inside these short windows; treat them as coarse activity samples, not evidence of peak compute or bandwidth saturation. Scheduler snapshots reached eight running and four waiting requests on every GPU.
All four bounded traces contain GPU kernels, and the complete instrumented output passed the frozen OCR, chunk and embedding check.
findings.next_step: Two proposals worsened the evaluator metrics and eight was effectively flat. Retain four and test shared region admission, with a round-robin control at the same capacity, to address the unequal GPU token work.
findings.optimization: After proposal depth, test assigning pending regions when a GPU has capacity. Current eager round-robin assignment balances counts but cannot move already assigned work from the slower GPU. Preserve output order and avoid reference-derived length estimates.
